statement: The four lemmas of the 3n-1 m-cycle template, on the negative side, with their constants derived rather than borrowed (collatz_3n_minus_1_m_cycles_note.md, Section 3). The map is g(y) = y/2 (even), (3y-1)/2 (odd) on the positive integers, the shortcut 3n+1 map on the negatives. (1) ODD RUNS: for odd y >= 3 with u = y - 1 and a = v_2(u), g^k(y) - 1 = (3/2)^k u for k <= a, the first a iterates are odd and g^a(y) is even; so a run of a odd steps starts at y >= 2^a + 1 (Hercher's Lemma 8 mirrored, floor larger by two, attained at 5 and 17) and its local maximum is at most u^delta + 1, delta = log_2 3. (2) CYCLE EQUATION: on a cycle with K steps and o odd steps and an even step, Lambda = o log 3 - K log 2 = -sum over odd y of log(1 - 1/(3y)) > 0, so 3^o > 2^K; a run from a local minimum y contributes less than 1/(y-1), hence Lambda < sum_i 1/(y_i - 1) <= m/(x_min - 1) for an m-cycle -- constant one where Hercher's Corollary 17 has 97/54, because the odd step subtracts. (3) CHAINING: consecutive local minima obey u_{i+1} < u_i^delta / 2 (tight on the 17-cycle: 16 -> 40 against 40.5), so o <= B(m) log_2 u_1 - (B(m) - m)/(delta - 1) with B(m) = (delta^m - 1)/(delta - 1), K < delta o, and log_2(x_min - 1) > L_min(K, m) = (K/delta + (B - m)/(delta - 1))/B. (4) ADMISSIBLE LENGTHS: above a floor X_0, Lambda(K) = log 3 (1 - frac(K x)) < m/(X_0 - 1), x = log 2/log 3, and the lengths with that property are enumerated exactly by the three-gap walk. Checked: the run identity and run length on every odd y < 4000, the cycle equation in exact rationals on the three cycles, the run reciprocal bound (worst ratio 0.988 of its limit 1 over that range). Not a halt theorem and not about the Juggler: the Juggler's cycle words are these cycles' words, but a word shape does not transport a realization.

SUPERSEDED 21 September 2026 by J-negative-m-cycles-excluded-through-58: the floor moved from 2^44 to 2^51 (GPU sweep) and the same tables read m <= 58. Kept as the record of the first draft. THEOREM, WITH ONE EXTERNAL INPUT. Given Rhin's effective measure |u_0 + u_1 log 2 + u_2 log 3| >= H^(-13.3) for H = max(|u_1|, |u_2|) >= 2 (Rhin 1987, Proposition p. 160 (7), read on 21 September 2026: no further constant; the form exp(-13.3 (0.46057 + log K_odd)) the laboratory carried since Paper A is Simons-de Weger 2005 Lemma 12, the same bound at H = K + L, weaker by delta^13.3 = 457 when H is the length itself), the 3n-1 map has no m-cycle with 1 <= m <= 49 whose least element is at least 2^44, and by the laboratory's floor (J-negative-floor-makes-the-mirror-unconditional) no m-cycle with m <= 49 other than (5, 7, 10) and the eleven-element cycle at 17. PROOF: Rhin's bound with J-negative-m-cycle-lemmas (2) and (3) gives 2^L_min(K, m) < m K^13.3, so every m-cycle has length below a ceiling K_3(m), the larger root of a convex function; below the ceiling the admissible lengths, Lambda(K) < m/(2^44 - 1), are enumerated exactly by the three-gap walk and each is tested against the chaining, 2^L_min(K, m) >= m/Lambda(K), at eighty digits. For m <= 43 no admissible length lies below the ceiling at all; for 44 <= m <= 49 the admissible lengths (1, 3, ..., 25 of them) are all excluded, the closest by 1.4 bits at m = 49, K = 757698850864. WHAT THE TEMPLATE LEAVES: at m = 50 the lengths 539722056247, 757698850864, 975675645481, 1193652440098 survive with 22.4, 15.0, 7.8 and 2.9 bits of room -- the near-convergent lengths of log 2/log 3 on the expanding side, the output of the template's last step, not its input: the floors that remove them are 2^44.01, 2^44.57, 2^45.48 and 2^48.58. THE FLOORS, by the same tables (COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED): 2^40 gives m <= 44, 2^48 still 49, 2^60 gives 68, and AT SIMONS-DE WEGER'S OWN FLOOR 301 * 2^50 (Roosendaal, November 2004; the earlier record's 2.5 * 2^60 was Simons 2008's later floor) the transposition gives m <= 63 with the first open length 766512153894657 at m = 64, (their ladder there: tables 57, continued fractions 63, lattice 68; CORRECTED 21 September 2026, second pass, after re-reading their Section 7: the three-gap walk IS their approximation lattice, a two-dimensional lattice whose short points are the (K, L) pairs in the Corollary 5 window below the ceiling, each then tested against Corollary 5 and Lemma 7, the two tests applied here; run on THEIR side with the window on the contracting side at their floor, the same machinery reproduces their Lemma 18 to the unit, none for 64 <= m <= 68 and their five pairs at 69 <= m <= 72 with their killing floors to rounding, 576.2/584.6/592.9/601.3 * 2^50 against their 577/585/593/602 for the first pair, plus the double of their second pair at m = 72 which their table omits; so no fifth step is left, and the five values between 63 and 68 are the sign of the map, the length 766512153894657 sitting inside the window on the expanding side at m = 64 while the contracting side has nothing below the ceiling until m = 69); 2^49, 2^50, 2^51 and 2^56 give 54, 56, 58 and 63, the first three also sieved independently; 2^68 gives 82 against Hercher's 91 at 695 * 2^60 with the valley arrangement, which is therefore worth about nine values of m and is the next refinement to transpose. THE KNOWN-BAD INPUTS: with the floor at 17 and m = 2 the template leaves the 17-cycle's length 11; at 5 and m = 1 it leaves length 3; one above each it does not. PRIORITY: Simons 2007 proves m = 2 floor-free and says the method stops at m >= 3; Simons-de Weger 2005 and Hercher 2023 are 3n+1 only; Simons 2008 skips the map; a search by name on 21 September 2026 found nothing else; Simons-de Weger 2005 read in full the same day. Not a halt theorem for either map, no Juggler cycle excluded, nothing about divergence.

Kept as the record of version 1.0.0 of the paper, which states m <= 58 and is correct as it stands. THEOREM, WITH ONE EXTERNAL INPUT. Given Rhin's effective measure |u_0 + u_1 log 2 + u_2 log 3| >= H^(-13.3) for H = max(|u_1|, |u_2|) >= 2 (Rhin 1987, Proposition p. 160 (7)), the 3n-1 map g(y) = y/2 (even), (3y-1)/2 (odd) has no m-cycle with 1 <= m <= 58 whose least element is at least 2^51; with the floor (every 1 <= y < 2^51 reaches 1, 5 or 17: the CPU certificate to 2^44 and the GPU sweep of 21 September 2026 to 2^51, 1117103813820416 odd starts, no failure, spot-checked against the CPU walker on three 2^37 windows), none with m <= 58 other than (5, 7, 10) and the cycle at 17. THE ROUTE is that of the m <= 49 row at 2^44 (J-negative-m-cycles-excluded-through-49, now superseded): negative Lemma 8 y >= 2^a + 1, the run identity, the cycle equation Lambda < m/(x_min - 1), the chaining u' < u^delta / 2, the exact enumeration of the admissible lengths by the three-gap walk below Rhin's ceiling K_3(m), each tested against the chaining; the enumeration is Simons-de Weger's Section 7 lattice list and the two tests are their Corollary 5 and Lemma 7, so no step of their template is left. AT 2^51: no admissible length below the ceiling for m <= 52; for 53 <= m <= 58 the admissible lengths (1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 16 of them) are excluded by the chaining, the closest with 9.8 bits to spare at m = 58, K = 64789416887513; at m = 59 two lengths survive, 64789416887513 (12.4 bits) and 83130157078217 (5.0 bits), removed at floors 2^51.87 and 2^55.18. THE LADDER by the same tables: 2^40 gives 44, 2^44 gives 49, 2^49 gives 54, 2^50 gives 56, 2^51 to 2^55 give 58, 2^56 gives 63, 2^59 gives 64, 2^60 gives 68, 2^68 gives 82; on the 3n+1 side at 301 * 2^50 the same machinery reproduces Simons-de Weger's Lemma 18 to the unit. The m-free period bound at 2^51 is 85137581 with 53715833 odd steps. INDEPENDENT CHECK: tools/check_3n_minus_1_note_numeric.py re-sieves the admissible lengths and recomputes the ceilings, margins and killing floors from scratch and agrees with the note's tables at this floor. THE KNOWN-BAD INPUTS: with the floor at 17 and m = 2 the template leaves the 17-cycle's length 11; at 5 and m = 1 it leaves length 3; one above each it does not. PRIORITY: Simons 2007 proves m = 2 floor-free; Simons-de Weger 2005 and Hercher 2023 do 3n+1; nothing in print does 3n-1 at any m >= 3. LEMMAS 1 AND 3 ARE LEAN (21 September 2026): Problems.Collatz.NegativeMCycles, twenty declarations, in the Problems barrel; thirteen on Mathlib's three standard axioms, five (the decide computations on the known cycles) on none, two derived; no sorry, no native_decide. The run is put in closed form as negT_run_iter, g^k(2^a m + 1) = 3^k 2^(a-k) m + 1 for k <= a, which removes every truncated subtraction; Lemma 1's clauses are negT_run_odd, negT_run_even, negT_start_ge, negT_localMax, packaged by negT_lemma_one over the v_2 decomposition negT_run_decomp, and Lemma 3 is negT_chain_nat (2 u' < 3^a m) with negT_chain_real (u' < u^delta / 2), packaged as negT_lemma_three. The sign of the map and the three known cycles are kernel computations (negT_sign_is_minus: g 17 = 25 where 3n+1 gives 26; negT_chain_tight_at_17: 2 * 40 < 81, one unit of slack, the note's tightness remark). FORMALIZING SHARPENED ONE HYPOTHESIS: the closed form needs no parity assumption on m, the powers of two alone keeping the state odd through the run, so oddness is used only to know the run stops at a. LEMMA 2 IS NOT IN LEAN: the cycle equation and the bound on Lambda are real-analytic; its first clause Lambda > 0 is neg_cycle_expanding on the conjugate side, and the conjugation x = -y is not formalized because Problems.Collatz sits below Problems.Juggler.

THEOREM, WITH ONE EXTERNAL INPUT. Given Rhin's effective measure |u_0 + u_1 log 2 + u_2 log 3| >= H^(-13.3) for H = max(|u_1|, |u_2|) >= 2 (Rhin 1987, Proposition p. 160 (7)), the 3n-1 map g(y) = y/2 (even), (3y-1)/2 (odd) has no m-cycle with 1 <= m <= 61 whose least element is at least 2^51; with the floor (every 1 <= y < 2^51 reaches 1, 5 or 17: the CPU certificate to 2^44 and the GPU sweep of 21 September 2026 to 2^51, 1117103813820416 odd starts, no failure, spot-checked against the CPU walker on three 2^37 windows), none with m <= 61 other than (5, 7, 10) and the cycle at 17. Paper D version 1.1.0, docs/theory/collatz_3n_minus_1_m_cycles_note.md. THE ROUTE is that of the m <= 58 row (J-negative-m-cycles-excluded-through-58, now superseded) with a sixth lemma: negative Lemma 8 y >= 2^a + 1, the run identity, the cycle equation Lambda < m/(x_min - 1), the chaining u' < u^delta / 2, the exact enumeration of the admissible lengths by the three-gap walk below Rhin's ceiling K_3(m), the contracting-prefix sieve, and now the valley count; each admissible length is tested against two displays and excluded if either holds. THE NEW LEMMA (Lemma 6 of the manuscript) is the transposition of the arrangement behind Hercher's Main Theorem 21. The earlier lemmas relax the same system twice, once by putting every local minimum at the floor and once by dropping the objective, and both relaxations are loose at the same time because a cycle cannot have all its valleys at the floor and carry o odd steps. Writing b_i = log2 u_i over the local minima, the constraints are b_i >= L0 = log2(X0 - 1), b_{i+1} < delta b_i - 1 (Lemma 3) and sum b_i >= o (Lemma 1 summed), with Lambda < sum 2^(-b_i) (Lemma 2) the objective. The lemma keeps them together through a threshold rather than a vertex enumeration: for every T >= L0, at most R(T) of the minima lie at or below T, where R(T) is the largest r <= m with r T + sum_{t <= m-r} (delta^t T - (delta^t - 1)/(delta - 1)) >= o, the largest total the chaining allows once the gaps between the low minima are merged into one; then Lambda < R(T) 2^(-L0) + (m - R(T)) 2^(-T). The minimum over T is exact rather than a grid: the bound is piecewise in T with breakpoints T_r = (o + A_{m-r}) / (r + B_{m-r}) and falls with T on each piece. At T = L0 it is Lemma 2, so the refinement is never weaker than what it refines. AT 2^51: no admissible length below the ceiling for m <= 52; for 53 <= m <= 61 the admissible lengths are excluded, the closest with 0.1 bits to spare at m = 61, K = 83130157078217; at m = 62 that same length survives with 0.3 bits. The theorem is delicate at its top end, which the two figures say plainly. THE LADDER by the same tables: 2^40 gives 49, 2^44 gives 51, 2^48 and 2^49 give 58, 2^50 gives 59, 2^51 gives 61, 2^56 gives 68, 301*2^50 gives 69, 2^60 gives 74, 2^68 gives 89, against 44, 49, 49, 54, 56, 58, 63, 63, 68 and 82 for the same floors without Lemma 6. The m-free period bound at 2^51 is unchanged at 85137581 with 53715833 odd steps. THE CALIBRATION, which is the evidence the transposition is faithful: run on the 3n+1 side at Hercher's own floor 695 * 2^60 the same six lemmas exclude m <= 90, one short of his published m <= 91 (Main Theorem 23) reached by the same idea. The comparison against Simons-de Weger's 68 is not the right one: their 2005 work predates the valley argument entirely, and at their floor 301*2^50 these lemmas give 69. INDEPENDENT CHECK: tools/check_3n_minus_1_note_numeric.py re-sieves the admissible lengths and recomputes the ceilings, margins and killing floors from scratch, with its own implementation of the valley cap written from the manuscript rather than imported from the probe, and agrees with the note's tables at this floor. THE KNOWN-BAD INPUTS: with the floor at their own least element the cycles (5, 7, 10) and 17 both clear the cap, so the refinement does not exclude the cycles that exist; the cap is separately checked never to exceed Lemma 2's m/(X0 - 1). PRIORITY: Simons 2007 proves m = 2 floor-free; Simons-de Weger 2005 and Hercher 2023 do 3n+1; nothing in print does 3n-1 at any m >= 3. LEAN, UNCHANGED BY THIS VERSION: Lemmas 1 and 3 are Problems.Collatz.NegativeMCycles, twenty declarations, no sorry and no native_decide; they are exactly the two the valley count consumes, so the formalized part of the route did not move. Lemma 2 remains real-analytic and unformalized, and Lemma 6 is arithmetic on top of 1, 2 and 3. MEASURED AND REJECTED on the way: Hercher's Corollary 29 (residue tracking) buys 1.30 bits where 4.18 are needed, and his Theorem 27 (m-free) is 0.23 bits tighter and leaves the period bound unchanged; both are method walls on this side, not oversights.
